svg.title: Project S.P.H.E.R.E. Seven-Tier Document and Evidence Authority Hierarchy
svg.desc: Seven-tier precedence stack showing how conflicts between documents are resolved: Tier 1 Immutable OSF LOC-1 preregistration, Tier 2 Dated pre-confirmatory amendments filed before data inspection, Tier 3 Controlled Versioned Whitepaper v2.0, Tier 4 Qualification and technical supplements, Tier 5 Website research and educational articles, Tier 6 FAQ, glossary, transcripts, and social copy, and Tier 7 Third-party AI reviews which are never authoritative.
svg.text: Figure 2 · Seven-Tier Document & Evidence Precedence Hierarchy
When sources conflict, higher tiers govern. Lower tiers may summarize or propose amendments but never silently override higher-tier records.
TIER 1
Immutable Registered LOC-1 Protocol & OSF Snapshot (osf.io/5b6mj/overview)
Binding confirmatory baseline. Never silently edited, overwritten, or backdated; governs Phase 1 confirmatory claims.
TIER 2
Explicit Dated Protocol Amendments Filed Before Confirmatory Data Inspection
e.g., Draft Amendment LOC-1A (currently DRAFT — not yet submitted to OSF; takes effect only if registered before unblinding).
TIER 3
Current Controlled Versioned Whitepaper (SPHERE-WP-001 v2.0, 2026-11-24)
Supersedes Zenodo v1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23583932) and internal v1.6. Explicitly flags every proposed delta vs. Tier 1.
TIER 4
Qualification Reports, Uncertainty Budgets & Technical Supplements
Empirical noise-floor, thermal calibration, MAC, and Allan-deviation records generated prior to confirmatory freeze.
TIER 5
Website Research Articles, Knowledge Base & Learn Guides (/research/, /knowledge/, /learn/)
Educational and methodological exposition; Phase 2 articles (record-replay, 4-object array) do NOT amend registered LOC-1.
TIER 6
FAQs, Glossary, Video Transcripts, Visual Lab (SPHEREVL L0) & Promotional Metadata
Must stay synchronized with Tiers 1–3; never introduce stronger claims than the governing whitepaper or OSF protocol.
TIER 7
Third-Party AI Reviews & Local LLM Outputs — NEVER AUTHORITATIVE
Used only as editorial checklists or critique prompts. Every factual scientific, legal, regulatory, financial, or standards claim
MUST be independently verified against a primary or authoritative standard before publication.
